subject: Phased rollout: custom SLA addendum & latency credit schedule
messages:
From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@healthlytix.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthlytix.com
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA addendum for phased rollout + latency credits

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's routing and caching story. We have an upcoming pilot (Phase 1) that is timeboxed to 4 weeks and limited to a subset of our users, followed by a ramp to full production (Phase 2) over 8–12 weeks. Before we kick off procurement, our legal and infra teams asked for a custom SLA addendum that covers two items specifically:

- Phased rollout language that limits the pilot to lower availability and defines transition criteria to prod (we need explicit acceptance gates).
- A latency credit schedule: for text generation p95 latency, we need clear p95 targets and a graduated credit schedule if targets are missed during Phase 2 (pilot tolerances are more lenient).

For reference, our target for production would be 99.95% availability and p95 <= 150ms for short-text generation under nominal load. Pilot tolerances: 99.5% availability and p95 <= 350ms. We understand custom SLAs have operational cost implications — please outline what evidence you need from us (SOC2, network topology, expected QPS) and any constraints on order form language.

I've attached a short security + infra questionnaire (HealthLytix_Security_QA.xlsx) and copied procurement. Could you provide a redline-ready addendum and a sample latency-credit table this week? We have a board date in late March and need these in hand for signatures.

Best,
Amir
Amir Khan
Head of Platform
HealthLytix
(amir.khan@healthlytix.com)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Amir Khan <amir.khan@healthlytix.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum for phased rollout + latency credits

Thanks Amir — appreciate the clarity and the questionnaire.

Quick responses / plan:
1) We can do a phased-rollout annex that explicitly defines Phase 1 (pilot) acceptance gates: user-sampled quality checks + operational metrics (availability & p95). We typically codify the transition as a joint runbook sign-off (CS + customer).
2) Latency-credit schedule — we have a few proven templates. Example approach we propose:
   - Phase 1 (pilot): 99.5% availability, p95 <= 350ms. Failure: operational remediation plan + up to 5% credit of monthly invoice for severity/impact.
   - Phase 2 (production ramp): 99.9% availability for the first 4 weeks after go-live, moving to 99.95% after 8 weeks. p95 target 150ms; misses are measured weekly with credits scaled by magnitude and recurrence (tiered: minor/major/repeat).

I looped in Karthik (legal/procurement) to draft order-form language and Monica (CS) to draft the operational acceptance gates and runbook template. Karthik — can you confirm if Redwood needs the SOC2 PDF + network topology + expected QPS breakdown in order to approve the 99.95% target for Phase 2?

Amir — we will get a redline-ready addendum and a sample credit table by EOD Monday. If you can confirm a preferred credit cap (percentage of MRR) that helps speed approval.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Amir Khan <amir.khan@healthlytix.com>, procurement@healthlytix.com
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum for phased rollout + latency credits

Folks — attaching suggested order-form and addendum language in-line below (I'll follow up with a tracked doc):

- Pilot/Phase language (simple): "Phase 1 (Pilot) shall be limited to the test environment and a capped user cohort as set forth in the Order Form. Service availability and latency targets for Phase 1 are set at the lower thresholds described in the Order Form; Phase 1 does not constitute the commencement of the Production Service Period until both parties have executed the acceptance checklist."

- Latency credit approach (high-level):
  * Credits are calculated as percentage of monthly fees for the impacted service tier.
  * For production (Phase 2):\n    - Single-week p95 breach >150ms but <=250ms: 2% credit; >250ms but <=400ms: 6% credit; >400ms: 12% credit.
    - Repeat breach (3+ occurrences in a rolling 12-week window): escalate to remediation SLA and larger credits (up to 25% with C-suite escalation).
  * For pilot (Phase 1): proportional but capped at 5% per month.

Evidence requirements before we commit to 99.95%: SOC2 Type II report (latest), documented maintenance windows, expected QPS and concurrency profile, and confirmation of any on-customer-network dependencies (edge proxies, NAT mapping). If HealthLytix requires HSM/KMS integrations, we'll need the KMS approval timeline documented.

I'll put the draft into DocuSign-friendly Word and send a link. Rafael / Monica — happy to iterate on the credit tiers if HealthLytix proposes different risk sharing.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal & Procurement, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
